title: Konuşma Pratikleri
description: Akıcı İngilizce için günlük pratik senaryoları. Her egzersiz gerçek iş hayatından alınmış durumları simüle eder.

exercises.title: 2-Minute Self Introduction
exercises.instructions_tr: Kendini 2 dakikada tanıt. Adın, geçmişin, ne üzerinde çalıştığın ve nereye gitmek istediğini anlat. Ezberleme — ana noktaları bil ve doğal konuş.
exercises.template_en: Hi, I'm [name]. I graduated from [school] with a degree in [field]. Over the past [time], I've been focusing on [skills/technologies]. I've built a few projects — the one I'm most proud of is [project], where I [what you did]. What excites me most about software development is [passion]. Right now, I'm looking for opportunities where I can [goal] and grow as an engineer.
tips_tr: Ezberlemek yerine 4-5 ana noktayı bil ve doğal konuş
Göz teması kur (video görüşmede kameraya bak, ekrana değil)
1-2 somut örnek ver — 'I built X using Y' gibi
'Um' ve 'like' gibi dolgu kelimelerden kaçın — sessizlik daha iyi
Sonunda ne aradığını net söyle — 'I'm looking for...' ile bitir
follow_up_questions: What's the most challenging project you've worked on?
Why did you choose this particular tech stack?
Where do you see yourself in 2-3 years?
What got you interested in software development in the first place?

exercises.title: Explain Your Current Project
exercises.instructions_tr: Şu anda üzerinde çalıştığın projeyi 3 dakikada açıkla. Projenin ne yaptığını, hangi teknolojileri kullandığını, mimari kararlarını ve karşılaştığın zorlukları anlat.
exercises.template_en: So the project I've been working on is [name/description]. Basically, it's a [type of app] that lets users [main functionality]. On the backend, I'm using [tech stack] — I chose [technology] because [reason]. The frontend is built with [framework]. One interesting challenge I ran into was [challenge]. I solved it by [solution]. If I were to do it again, I'd probably [improvement]. Overall, I've learned a ton about [learning area].
tips_tr: 'Basically, it's a...' ile başla — karmaşık şeyleri basitleştir
Neden o teknolojiyi seçtiğini açıkla — 'I chose X because...'
Bir zorluktan ve nasıl çözdüğünden bahset — bu en ilginç kısım
Ne öğrendiğini ve neyi farklı yapardığını ekle
3 dakikayı geçme — özlü ol
follow_up_questions: What was the hardest bug you encountered?
How would you scale this if it had 10x users?
What would you change about the architecture?
Did you consider any alternative technologies?

exercises.title: Describe a Bug You Fixed (STAR Method)
exercises.instructions_tr: Çözdüğün ilginç bir bug'ı STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) yöntemiyle anlat. Durumu kısaca anlat, ne yapman gerektiğini, nasıl yaklaştığını ve sonucu açıkla.
exercises.template_en: So this was back when I was working on [project]. [Situation:] We started getting reports from users that [symptom]. [Task:] I was assigned to figure out what was going on and fix it. [Action:] The first thing I did was check the logs, and I noticed [observation]. That led me to suspect [hypothesis]. I dug deeper and found that [root cause]. The fix involved [solution]. [Result:] After deploying the fix, [positive outcome]. We also added [preventive measure] to make sure it wouldn't happen again.
tips_tr: Durumu 2-3 cümlede anlat — uzatma
Debug sürecini adım adım anlat — düşünce sürecini göster
Kök nedeni bulmayı vurgula — 'The root cause turned out to be...'
Sonucu somut rakamlarla ver — '99.9% uptime' gibi
Önleyici tedbir eklediğinden bahset — olgunluk gösterir
follow_up_questions: How long did it take you to find the root cause?
What tools did you use for debugging?
What would you do differently next time?
How did you prevent this from happening again?

exercises.title: Explain a Technical Concept to Non-Technical Person
exercises.instructions_tr: Teknik bir kavramı (API, veritabanı, Docker, CI/CD gibi) teknik bilgisi olmayan birine anlat. Jargon kullanma, analoji ve günlük hayattan örnekler kullan.
exercises.template_en: Okay, so imagine you're at a restaurant. [Analogy setup]. An API is basically like the waiter — you don't go into the kitchen and talk to the chef directly. Instead, you tell the waiter what you want, the waiter takes your order to the kitchen, and brings back your food. In software, an API works the same way. Your app doesn't directly access the database or another service — it sends a request through the API, and the API brings back the data. The menu is like the API documentation — it tells you what you can order and how to order it.
tips_tr: 'Imagine you're at...' veya 'Think of it like...' ile başla
Bir analoji seç ve ona bağlı kal — karıştırma
Teknik terimleri günlük kelimelere çevir
'Does that make sense?' diye sor — anlaşıldığını kontrol et
Karşı tarafın 'aha' anını hedefle
follow_up_questions: Can you give me a real-world example of this?
Why is this important for our product?
What happens if this breaks?
How does this affect the user experience?

exercises.title: Give a Standup Update
exercises.instructions_tr: 30 saniyede standup update'ini ver. Dün ne yaptığını, bugün ne yapacağını ve varsa engelleri bildir. Kısa, net ve yapılandırılmış ol.
exercises.template_en: Yesterday I [completed task]. I also spent some time on [secondary task]. Today I'm going to [plan for today]. I'm aiming to have [deliverable] ready by [time]. [If blocker:] One thing — I'm blocked on [blocker]. I need [what you need] from [who] to move forward. [If no blocker:] No blockers on my end.
tips_tr: 30 saniyeyi geçme — herkes bekliyor
Yaptığın işi geçmiş zamanda anlat: 'I finished', 'I completed'
Bugünkü planı gelecek zamanda anlat: 'I'm going to', 'I'll be working on'
Blocker varsa kime ihtiyacın olduğunu net söyle
Detaylara girme — 'I can give more details after standup' de
follow_up_questions: Do you need help with anything?
Is that going to be ready for the demo on Friday?
Can you give a rough estimate on the remaining work?
Should we reprioritize anything based on this?

exercises.title: Propose a Technical Solution
exercises.instructions_tr: Bir teknik soruna çözüm öner. Problemi tanımla, önerdiğin çözümü açıkla, alternatifleri ele al ve neden bu yaklaşımı seçtiğini savun.
exercises.template_en: So the problem we're facing is [problem description]. We've got a few options here. Option A is [first approach] — the upside is [benefit], but the downside is [drawback]. Option B is [second approach] — it's [comparison to A]. My recommendation is Option [choice], and here's why: [reasoning]. The implementation would take roughly [timeline]. We'd need to [dependencies]. The main risk is [risk], but we can mitigate that by [mitigation]. Any questions or concerns?
tips_tr: Problemi net tanımla — herkes aynı sayfada olmalı
En az 2 alternatif sun — tek seçenek sunma
Her seçeneğin artı ve eksilerini belirt
Önerini gerekçelendir — 'My recommendation is X because...'
Riskleri proaktif olarak ele al — 'The main risk is... but we can mitigate...'
Zaman tahmini ver — 'roughly 2 sprints'
follow_up_questions: What happens if this doesn't work as expected?
Have you considered the scalability implications?
What's the minimum viable version of this?
How would we roll this back if something goes wrong?

exercises.title: Disagree with a Technical Decision
exercises.instructions_tr: Bir teknik kararla kibar ama kararlı bir şekilde katılmadığını ifade et. Karşı tarafın argümanını kabul et, kendi perspektifini sun, kanıtlarla destekle.
exercises.template_en: I see where you're coming from with [their approach], and I understand the appeal — [acknowledge their reasoning]. That said, I have some concerns about [specific concern]. In my experience, [counter-example or evidence]. I'd actually suggest we consider [your alternative] instead, because [reasoning]. The trade-off would be [what you'd give up], but I think that's worth it because [justification]. What do you think? Am I missing something?
tips_tr: Her zaman karşı tarafın argümanını kabul ederek başla
'You're wrong' asla deme — 'I have some concerns about...' de
Kişisel deneyimden örnek ver — 'In my experience...'
Alternatif sun — sadece eleştirme, çözüm de öner
'What do you think? Am I missing something?' ile bitir — diyalog davet et
Ego savaşına girme — doğru çözümü bulmaya odaklan
follow_up_questions: What evidence do you have to support your approach?
Have you seen this work in production at scale?
What's the worst case scenario with your approach?
Can we run a quick proof of concept to test both?

exercises.title: Ask for a Code Review
exercises.instructions_tr: PR'ını açtın ve takımdan review istemen gerekiyor. Değişikliklerini kısaca özetle, neye dikkat etmelerini söyle ve ne zaman review yapabileceklerini sor.
exercises.template_en: Hey [name], I just put up a PR for [feature/fix]. It's a [size — small/medium/large] change — about [number] files touched. Here's the TL;DR: [1-2 sentence summary]. I'm particularly looking for feedback on [specific area]. The tests are all passing and I've tested it manually in staging. No rush, but if you could take a look by [time], that'd be great. Let me know if you have any questions — happy to walk through the code.
tips_tr: PR'ın büyüklüğünü belirt — reviewer'ın zamanını planlamasına yardımcı olur
'TL;DR' ile kısa özet ver — kimse uzun açıklama okumak istemez
Hangi konuda özellikle feedback istediğini söyle
Testlerin geçtiğini belirt — güven verir
'No rush, but by [time]' ile beklentini ilet
follow_up_questions: Is there a specific part you're unsure about?
Did you consider any alternative approaches?
Are there any breaking changes I should know about?
Should I test anything specific before approving?

exercises.title: Report a Production Incident
exercises.instructions_tr: Production'da bir sorun var ve bunu Slack'te takıma rapor etmen gerekiyor. Net, kısa ve yapılandırılmış ol. Ne olduğunu, etkisini, şu ana kadar ne yaptığını ve ne zaman güncelleyeceğini bildir.
exercises.template_en: [Severity] Incident: [Brief description]. Impact: [Who is affected and how]. Timeline: First reports came in at [time]. What we know so far: [findings]. Current status: [what you're doing right now]. Next update in [time]. I'll keep this thread updated. [If help needed:] Could use a hand with [specific ask].
tips_tr: İlk mesajda 4 şeyi kapsayın: ne oldu, kim etkilendi, ne yapıyorsun, ne zaman güncelleyeceksin
Panik yapma — sakin ve olgusal yaz
Thread kullan — ana kanalı spam'leme
Düzenli güncelleme ver — 'Still investigating' bile yeterli
Suçlama yapma — çözüme odaklan
Çözüldüğünde 'Resolved' mesajı at ve kısa özet ver
follow_up_questions: What's the blast radius of this?
Do we need to notify affected users?
Should we roll back or push a hotfix?
Who else should we loop in?

exercises.title: Explain Why You Chose React Over Angular
exercises.instructions_tr: Bir teknoloji seçimini gerekçelendir. Neden React'i (veya başka bir teknolojiyi) seçtiğini, alternatifleri neden eledini ve hangi kriterlere göre karar verdiğini açıkla.
exercises.template_en: Great question. So when I was evaluating frontend frameworks, I looked at three main criteria: [criterion 1], [criterion 2], and [criterion 3]. React stood out because [reason 1]. Compared to Angular, it has a [advantage] — for example, [concrete example]. That said, Angular has its strengths too, especially [Angular strength]. But for our use case — [specific context] — React was the better fit because [specific reason]. The ecosystem was also a factor — [ecosystem benefit]. If we were building [different type of app], I might've gone with [alternative] instead.
tips_tr: Fanboy gibi konuşma — 'React is the best' deme
Kriterleri belirle ve nesnel karşılaştır
Alternatiflerin güçlü yanlarını da kabul et
'For our use case' de — bağlama özel karar ver
Farklı bir durumda farklı seçim yapacağını göster — olgunluk
follow_up_questions: What are the main drawbacks of your choice?
How would you migrate if you needed to switch?
What about newer options like Svelte or Solid?
How does this choice affect hiring?

exercises.title: Describe Your Ideal Team Culture
exercises.instructions_tr: İdeal takım kültürünü tanımla. Nasıl bir ortamda en iyi çalıştığını, hangi değerlere önem verdiğini ve geçmiş deneyimlerinden örnekler ver.
exercises.template_en: For me, the ideal team culture is one where people feel safe to speak up and make mistakes. I really value [value 1] — like, if I push a bug to production, I want the response to be 'let's fix it and learn from it,' not 'whose fault is this?' I also care a lot about [value 2]. In my experience, teams that [positive behavior] tend to ship better code. One thing I've seen work really well is [specific practice]. On the flip side, I struggle in environments where [negative trait]. At the end of the day, I want to work with people who are [qualities] and who genuinely enjoy what they do.
tips_tr: Somut örnekler ver — soyut konuşma
Geçmiş deneyimlerinden referans ver
Hem istediğin hem istemediğin şeyleri söyle
Blameless culture, psychological safety gibi kavramlara değin
Gerçekçi ol — 'ping pong masası' değil, gerçek değerlerden bahset
follow_up_questions: How do you handle conflict within a team?
What does 'psychological safety' look like in practice?
How do you give feedback to teammates?
What's the most dysfunctional team you've been on and what did you learn?

exercises.title: Walk Through Your GitHub Portfolio
exercises.instructions_tr: GitHub portföyünü gezdirerek projelerini anlat. En önemli 2-3 projeyi seç, ne yaptıklarını, hangi teknolojileri kullandığını ve ne öğrendiğini açıkla.
exercises.template_en: Sure, let me walk you through my GitHub. So the main projects you'll see here are [project 1], [project 2], and [project 3]. Let's start with [project 1] — this is a [description]. I built it using [tech stack]. The most interesting part is [highlight]. If you look at the code, you'll notice I focused on [code quality aspect]. [Project 2] is a [description]. This one taught me a lot about [learning]. I'm most proud of [specific achievement]. I try to keep my repos well-documented — you'll see a README with setup instructions, architecture diagrams, and a contributing guide.
tips_tr: 2-3 projeye odaklan — hepsini anlatmaya çalışma
Her proje için: ne yaptığını, neden yaptığını, ne öğrendiğini anlat
Kod kalitesini vurgula — testler, CI/CD, dokümantasyon
Canlı demo varsa göster — çok etkili
README kalitesi önemli — buna değin
follow_up_questions: Which project are you most proud of and why?
What would you refactor if you had more time?
Do you have any contributions to open source?
How did you decide what to build?

exercises.title: Explain a System Design (URL Shortener)
exercises.instructions_tr: Basit bir URL kısaltıcı sistem tasarımını adım adım açıkla. Gereksinimleri tanımla, yüksek seviye mimariyi çiz, bileşenleri açıkla ve ölçeklendirme stratejisini anlat.
exercises.template_en: Alright, so let's design a URL shortener. First, let me clarify the requirements. We need to generate short URLs from long ones, redirect users when they visit the short URL, and track click analytics. For the high-level architecture, I'd go with [components]. The core flow would be: user submits a long URL, we generate a unique short code using [algorithm], store the mapping in [database], and return the short URL. For the redirect, when someone hits the short URL, we look up the mapping and send a 301 redirect. For scale, I'd add [caching strategy] in front of the database since reads will far outnumber writes. If we need to handle [scale], we could [scaling approach]. The tricky parts are [edge cases].
tips_tr: Gereksinimleri netleştirerek başla — 'Let me clarify the requirements'
Yüksek seviyeden başla, sonra detaylara in
Trade-off'ları tartış — 'The trade-off here is...'
Rakamlarla konuş — 'If we need to handle 1M URLs per day...'
Edge case'leri düşün — hash collision, expired URLs, abuse
Ölçeklendirme stratejisini anlat — caching, sharding, CDN
follow_up_questions: How would you handle hash collisions?
What happens if your database goes down?
How would you implement URL expiration?
What's your strategy for preventing abuse?

exercises.title: Give Feedback on Someone's Code
exercises.instructions_tr: Bir meslektaşının kodunu inceleyip yapıcı geri bildirim ver. Olumlu yönleri belirt, iyileştirme önerilerini nazikçe sun ve kararı onlara bırak.
exercises.template_en: Hey, I went through your PR and overall it's looking really solid. I especially liked how you [specific positive]. A couple of things I noticed: First, in [file/function], I think we could [improvement suggestion]. The reason is [reasoning]. It's not a blocker though — just a suggestion. Second, I noticed [potential issue]. Have you considered [alternative approach]? That might help with [benefit]. Other than that, the logic is clean and the tests look comprehensive. Nice work! Let me know what you think about those suggestions.
tips_tr: Her zaman pozitifle başla — 'Overall it's looking solid'
Spesifik ol — 'in line 42 of auth.ts' gibi
Önerini gerekçelendir — 'because...'
Blocker mı değil mi belirt — 'Not a blocker, just a suggestion'
'You should' yerine 'Have you considered...' veya 'What do you think about...' kullan
Kararı onlara bırak — 'Let me know what you think'
follow_up_questions: What was your reasoning behind this approach?
Did you consider any edge cases here?
Is there documentation for this new behavior?
Should we add a test for the error case?

exercises.title: Negotiate a Deadline
exercises.instructions_tr: Bir proje veya özellik için verilen sürenin gerçekçi olmadığını düşünüyorsun. Deadline'ı müzakere et — problemi açıkla, alternatifler sun, uzlaşmaya var.
exercises.template_en: I want to be upfront about the timeline for [feature]. The current deadline is [date], but after digging into the requirements, I think we're looking at [realistic timeline] to do this properly. Here's why: [specific reasons]. Now, I know the deadline is important, so here are some options. Option 1: We deliver the full feature by [later date]. Option 2: We ship a stripped-down version by [original date] with just [core features], and add [remaining features] in a follow-up sprint. Option 3: We bring in [additional resource] to speed things up, though there'll be a ramp-up period. I'd recommend Option [choice] because [reasoning]. What works best for the business?
tips_tr: 'I want to be upfront' ile başla — şeffaflık güven oluşturur
Neden geciktiğini somut sebeplerle açıkla
Sadece problem sunma — çözüm öner
En az 2-3 alternatif sun
Bir öneride bulun ama kararı karşı tarafa bırak
'What works best for the business?' ile bitir — iş odaklı düşündüğünü göster
Asla 'I can't do it' deme — 'Here's what we can do' de
follow_up_questions: What's the absolute minimum we need for launch?
What are the consequences of missing this deadline?
Can we reduce the scope without losing the core value?
Is there any part we can parallelize?

exercises.title: Feature Development Update
exercises.scenario: Sprint'in 3. günü. Kullanıcı profil sayfası üzerinde çalışıyorsun. Dün avatar yükleme özelliğini bitirdin, bugün profil düzenleme formuna geçeceksin.
exercises.prompt: Give your daily standup update. Cover what you did yesterday, what you plan for today, and any blockers.
exercises.example_response: Yesterday I finished the avatar upload feature — users can now crop and upload profile pictures. I also wrote unit tests for the image resize utility. Today I'm going to start on the profile edit form. I'll be building out the form validation and hooking it up to the API. I'm aiming to have the basic form working by end of day. No blockers on my end.
key_phrases: I finished...
I also wrote...
Today I'm going to start on...
I'll be building out...
I'm aiming to have... ready by...
No blockers on my end
exercises.follow_up: Can you estimate how many story points are left on the profile epic?
exercises.pronunciation_tip: 'Aiming' — /eɪ.mɪŋ/ — 'aim' kelimesindeki 'ai' sesi Türkçe'deki 'ey' gibi okunur, 'a-i' olarak değil.

exercises.title: Bug Fix Progress Report
exercises.scenario: Production'da kritik bir bug var — checkout sayfasında ödeme butonu bazı kullanıcılarda çalışmıyor. Dün root cause'u buldun, bugün fix'i deploy edeceksin.
exercises.prompt: Report your progress on the critical checkout bug in standup.
exercises.example_response: Yesterday I dug into the checkout button issue. I found the root cause — there was a race condition between the payment SDK initialization and the button render. The SDK was loading asynchronously but the button wasn't waiting for it. Today I'm going to implement the fix using a loading state and push it to staging for QA. If testing goes well, I'd like to deploy to production by this afternoon. No blockers, but I'll need someone from QA to verify the fix on staging.
key_phrases: I dug into...
I found the root cause...
There was a race condition between...
Today I'm going to implement the fix...
I'd like to deploy to production by...
I'll need someone from QA to verify...
exercises.follow_up: How many users are affected? Should we send a notification once it's fixed?
exercises.pronunciation_tip: 'Asynchronously' — /eɪˈsɪŋ.krə.nəs.li/ — 5 heceli zor bir kelime. 'A-SINK-ruh-nus-lee' olarak pratik yap.

exercises.title: Code Review Day
exercises.scenario: Dün kendi feature'ını tamamladın ama takım arkadaşlarının 3 PR'ı review bekliyor. Bugün code review'a odaklanacaksın.
exercises.prompt: Share your standup update focused on code review responsibilities.
exercises.example_response: Yesterday I wrapped up the notification service refactoring and opened a PR. Today I'm going to focus on code reviews — I've got three PRs in the queue. Sarah's authentication middleware change, Mike's database migration, and the new API versioning PR from Alex. I want to make sure we don't have a bottleneck before the sprint ends. I should be done with all three by early afternoon, then I'll pick up the caching ticket. No blockers.
key_phrases: I wrapped up...
I opened a PR
Today I'm going to focus on code reviews
I've got three PRs in the queue
I want to make sure we don't have a bottleneck
I should be done with... by...
exercises.follow_up: Are any of those PRs blocking someone else's work?
exercises.pronunciation_tip: 'Queue' — /kjuː/ — 'Q' harfinin okunuşuyla aynı. Türkler genelde 'kü-yü' der ama tek hece: 'kyoo'.

exercises.title: Deployment Day Update
exercises.scenario: Bugün büyük bir release deploy edeceksin. Dün son testleri tamamladın, staging'de her şey çalışıyor. Production deployment planını paylaşman gerekiyor.
exercises.prompt: Give your standup update about today's production deployment.
exercises.example_response: Yesterday I ran the final round of regression tests on staging — everything passed. I also did a dry run of the database migration and it completed in under 30 seconds. Today is deployment day. The plan is to start the production deploy at 2 PM during low-traffic hours. I'll run the migration first, then deploy the backend services, and finally the frontend. The whole process should take about 45 minutes. I've got the rollback scripts ready just in case. One thing — I'll need the on-call engineer to be available during the deploy window in case we need to roll back quickly.
key_phrases: I ran the final round of... tests
I did a dry run of...
The plan is to start... at...
during low-traffic hours
The whole process should take about...
I've got the rollback scripts ready
I'll need... to be available during...
exercises.follow_up: What's the rollback plan if the migration fails halfway through?

exercises.title: Blocked and Needs Help
exercises.scenario: 3. parti API entegrasyonunda takıldın. API dokümantasyonu eksik ve destek ekibinden cevap alamıyorsun. Yardıma ihtiyacın var.
exercises.prompt: Report that you're blocked in standup and ask for specific help.
exercises.example_response: Yesterday I started integrating the Stripe Connect API for marketplace payouts. I got the basic flow working, but I'm stuck on the account verification step. The documentation is unclear about how to handle the identity verification webhook, and I've been going back and forth with their support team with no clear answer. I'm blocked on this — I can't move forward with payouts until I figure out the verification flow. Could someone who's worked with Stripe Connect before take a quick look? Even 15 minutes of pairing would probably unblock me. In the meantime, I'll work on the payout dashboard UI so I'm not idle.
key_phrases: I started integrating...
I got the basic flow working, but I'm stuck on...
The documentation is unclear about...
I've been going back and forth with...
I'm blocked on this
Could someone who's worked with... take a quick look?
In the meantime, I'll work on...
exercises.follow_up: I've used Stripe Connect before. Let's pair after standup.

exercises.title: Multi-Task Sprint Day
exercises.scenario: Sprint'in son günü. Bir feature'ı bitirmen, bir bug fix yapman ve demo hazırlaman gerekiyor. Çok yoğun bir gün.
exercises.prompt: Give a structured standup update covering multiple priorities.
exercises.example_response: Yesterday I got about 80% through the search filters feature — just need to wire up the date range picker. I also started looking into the memory leak reported on the dashboard page. Today I've got three things on my plate. First priority is finishing the search filters since the demo is tomorrow. Second, I'll fix that memory leak — I'm pretty sure it's a missing cleanup in a useEffect hook. Third, I need to prepare the demo script and make sure the staging environment is up to date. It's a packed day but I think it's doable. No blockers, but if anyone could help test the search filters on staging later today, that would save me some time.

exercises.example_response: I need to flag a critical security concern on line 47. The user input is being interpolated directly into the SQL query string. Now, the trade-off: Server Components can't use state or effects — they're static. So you still need Client Components for interactive parts. The pattern is Server Components for data display, Client Components for interactivity.

exercises.example_response: I see what you're going for with that regex, and it would work. But can I suggest something? This might be a case where we're overcomplicating things. The input format is always 'name:value' pairs separated by semicolons, right? We could just split by semicolon, then split each pair by colon. Something like: input.split(';').map(pair => pair.split(':')).reduce((obj, [key, val]) => ({...obj, [key.trim()]: val.trim()}), {}). It's more readable, easier to debug if something breaks, and we don't have to worry about regex edge cases like escaped characters. The regex is clever, but six months from now, someone's going to look at it and have no idea what it does. What do you think? Am I missing an edge case that requires regex?

exercises.title: Learning from a Senior Developer
exercises.scenario: Senior developer ile pair yapıyorsun. O sürüyor ve bir design pattern uyguluyor. Ne yaptığını anlamak için sorular soruyorsun.
exercises.prompt: Ask good questions while learning from a senior developer during pairing.
exercises.example_response: This is really interesting. I see you're creating a separate class for each notification type — EmailNotification, SMSNotification, PushNotification. Is this the Strategy pattern? I'm curious about a few things. Why did you choose to use an interface here instead of an abstract class? Also, I noticed you're injecting the notification strategy into the NotificationService constructor. Is that dependency injection? What's the advantage of doing it this way versus just importing the class directly? And one more thing — how do you decide when to use a design pattern versus just writing straightforward code? I sometimes feel like I should be using patterns everywhere, but I'm not sure when it's actually worth the extra abstraction.

exercises.follow_up: Great questions! The rule of thumb is: if you need to swap behaviors at runtime, a pattern is worth it. Otherwise, keep it simple.

exercises.title: Handling Disagreement During Pairing
exercises.scenario: Sen ve pair partner'ın bir sorunun çözümü konusunda anlaşamıyorsunuz. O REST API istiyor, sen GraphQL'in daha uygun olacağını düşünüyorsun.
exercises.prompt: Navigate a disagreement about technical approach during pair programming.
exercises.example_response: I see the case for REST — it's simpler and our team already knows it well. But hear me out on why GraphQL might be a better fit for this specific endpoint. The dashboard page needs data from five different entities — users, orders, products, analytics, and notifications. With REST, that's five separate API calls. With GraphQL, it's one query that gets exactly the data we need. The dashboard is also mobile-responsive, and on mobile we'd want less data to save bandwidth. GraphQL lets us request fewer fields on mobile without creating a separate endpoint. Here's what I suggest: let's time-box this. Give me 20 minutes to set up a basic GraphQL query for the dashboard, and you build the equivalent REST endpoints. Then we compare the developer experience and the payload size. Data beats opinions. Fair?

exercises.title: Noticing a Potential Bug
exercises.scenario: Partner'ın sürerken bir potansiyel bug fark ediyorsun — off-by-one error. Şu an fark etmemiş, nazikçe belirtmen gerekiyor.
exercises.prompt: Point out a potential bug you noticed while navigating.
exercises.example_response: Hey, hold on a sec. Go back to line 23 — the for loop. I think there might be an off-by-one error. You're iterating from 0 to items.length, but you're using items[i + 1] inside the loop body. On the last iteration, when i equals length minus 1, items[i + 1] would be undefined, and calling .name on undefined will throw a TypeError. I think you either need to change the condition to i < items.length - 1, or add a bounds check inside the loop. Let's add a quick test for this — what happens when we pass an array with only one item? I bet it crashes.

Root cause: A memory leak in the payment processing worker caused the service to gradually consume all available memory, leading to out-of-memory crashes. The leak was introduced in deploy v2.4.7 this morning. Fix: We deployed a hotfix, v2.4.8, that properly disposes of payment gateway connections after each transaction. Follow-up actions: A post-mortem meeting is scheduled for tomorrow at 10 AM. All relevant team members will receive a calendar invite shortly.
